quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Technology and product webinar slides (led by President and Chief Technology and Products Officer Scott DeBoer): the next DRAM node, 1δ (1-delta), is described as 'the world's most advanced DRAM' and the 'fifth consecutive node of DRAM industry leadership' (Micron's claims), 'ramping in the second half of 2027'. Micron states 1δ delivers a mid-20s percentage bit density improvement from 1γ (1-gamma) with optimized cost, uses angstrom-level process control, equipment intelligence, new materials and advanced HKMG CMOS, is 'industry-leading technology manufactured in the U.S.', supports differentiated HBM5, vHBM (vertical HBM) and vEIM (vertical edge inference memory) products, and enables next-generation LPDDR, DDR and graphics modules (advanced TSV technology, thermal-aware design).
quarterly_data.figure: 1δ ramping in the second half of 2027; mid-20s percentage bit density improvement from 1γ

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DRAM technology roadmap (webinar slides): 'Micron is extending 6F² leadership and developing 3D DRAM; not pursuing 4F² due to increased complexity/cost' -- after 'over two decades of 4F² technology investigation', Micron sees 'no viable scaling path' for 4F². Micron says the DRAM cell is nearing atomic limits, so DRAM 'must now build up'. The 6F² roadmap runs from 1γ (in high-volume manufacturing) through 1δ, 1ε, ζÅ and ηÅ, alongside 3D DRAM generations 3D1 and 3D2, and the page 16 chart pairs each node with a phase and a milestone: 1γ in high-volume manufacturing (EUV introduction), 1δ yield ramp (U.S. manufactured), 1ε development (wafer bonding), ζÅ early development (High-NA EUV) and ηÅ pathfinding (new materials); the slide states 'Directional; no dates implied. Node names and phases subject to change.' A DRAM CMOS logic roadmap targets more than 10x CMOS logic performance from 2020 to 2030, moving from Poly SiON through three generations of HKMG to first- and second-generation 3D CMOS. Micron also states more than 400x more bits per DRAM wafer since 1995 across 22 Micron DRAM nodes (1995 to 2026).
quarterly_data.figure: not pursuing 4F²; >10x CMOS logic performance 2020 to 2030; >400x more bits per DRAM wafer since 1995; 22 DRAM nodes

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation DRAM for AI (webinar slides), stated as targets: LP6 for data center and mobile with more than 35% improved power versus LP5; high-reliability DDR6 for servers with more than 2x the bandwidth of DDR5; and a high-capacity 1TB RDIMM. The slide notes: 'Performance improvements are targets. 1 TB RDIMM is a capability, not a product commitment.'
quarterly_data.figure: >35% improved power vs. LP5 (LP6); >2x bandwidth vs. DDR5 (DDR6); 1TB RDIMM capability

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HBM product roadmap 2026-2030 (webinar slides): 'Product roadmap expands to custom HBM, vHBM and vEIM'. The chart lists HBM4, HBM4E, HBM5, HBM5E and HBM6, vHBM 1, 2 and 3 (vertical 3D HBM: memory stacked on compute, the shortest memory-compute path) and vEIM 1, 2 and 3 (vertical edge inference memory) by targeted high-volume-manufacturing year on the page 22 chart: HBM4 2026, HBM4E 2027, HBM5 2028, HBM5E 2029, HBM6 2030; vHBM 1, 2 and 3 in 2028, 2029 and 2030; vEIM 1, 2 and 3 in 2028, 2029 and 2030; HBM is 'JEDEC + custom beginning with HBM4E', with custom HBM co-designed with customers and base-die logic adding differentiated features. vEIM 1 specs: 2 TB/s bandwidth and <1 pJ/bit energy. The slide states 'Product timing represents targeted high-volume manufacturing; timing and performance targets are directional and subject to change.' Enablers named: hybrid bonding (higher stack density, finer interconnect pitch), advanced thermals and system co-design of base die, PHY, packaging and workload; packaging work includes TSV and µbump scaling, hybrid copper bonding, a 16H µbump and hybrid stack, 2.5D HBM + 3D vHBM integration and a heat spreader over the PHY.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4 2026, HBM4E 2027, HBM5 2028, HBM5E 2029, HBM6 2030; vHBM 1-3 and vEIM 1-3 in 2028-2030 (page 22 chart, targeted HVM, directional); vEIM 1: 2 TB/s bandwidth, <1 pJ/bit

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Micron's 2019-2026 technology-leadership timeline (webinar slides) lists, in its 2026 column (page 10 chart), 'HBM4E samples to key customers' (no customer named) and 'HBM4 12H shipments' alongside HBM3E 8H volume production and HBM3E 12H shipments, and claims 4 consecutive DRAM leadership nodes, 3 consecutive HBM generations of performance and power leadership and 3 consecutive NAND leadership nodes (Micron's claims). Micron states one HBM4 stack delivers 2.8 TB/s (2,048 bits x 11 Gbps).
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4E samples to key customers; one HBM4 stack 2.8 TB/s

quarterly_data.signal: Product milestones listed in the webinar slides (Micron: claims of industry leadership 'apply at the time of announcement and are not ongoing claims'): Jan 2026 shipped the 3610 SSD, 'industry-first PCIe Gen5 G9 QLC client SSD'; Mar 2026 sampled 256 GB SOCAMM2, 'industry's highest-capacity LPDRAM module'; Aug 2026 qualified ASIL-B UFS 4.1, 'world's first ASIL-B UFS 4.1 for automotive'; earlier, Mar 2025 shipped the industry-first SOCAMM module and Jun 2025 shipped samples of 1γ-based 10.7 Gbps LPDDR5X.

quarterly_data.signal: Co-innovation (webinar slides): 'Micron actively developing custom products with multiple CSPs' (cloud service providers, none named); Micron co-designs with foundry partners, uses an AI design workflow with EDA vendors and qualifies solutions together with customers and partners, optimizing base die, DRAM, interfaces, power and packaging.

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: LPDDR6 for data center systems (webinar slides): Micron is 'advancing LPDDR6 as data center-class memory architecture', combining 'Meta platform and application expertise' with Micron memory innovation for fleet-scale optimization, citing the Meta X Micron joint whitepaper 'LPDDR6: A Scalable, Power-Efficient Memory for Data Centers'. Customer challenge as Micron states it: power-efficient scaling of memory bandwidth is a primary need for advanced compute and AI.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: partner (LPDDR6 for data-center systems; joint whitepaper)

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI in Micron's own development (webinar slides, Micron internal program data, prior generation vs new generation): a data center SSD controller reached silicon tape-out 2x faster with AI (50% less time; AI-agent RTL and verification, GenAI IP porting, AI physical design), and a data center SSD product reached silicon ready for customer releases more than 2x faster (60% less time; AI-generated firmware, smart test selection, coverage agents). Micron's headline: 'AI makes Micron 2x faster: invention to volume production'.
quarterly_data.figure: SSD controller tape-out 2x faster (50% less time); SSD product >2x faster to customer-release silicon (60% less time)

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Long-horizon R&D investments (webinar slides): Micron Ventures has a $550M total capital commitment, investing across the AI stack to strengthen ecosystem engagement (3-10 year horizon); Micron works with Albany NanoTech and NY CREATES to accelerate the high-NA EUV and lithography roadmap (5-10 year horizon); Micron Research Labs (10+ year horizon) is the first dedicated memory research hub in the U.S. per Micron.

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Micron's framing of AI memory demand (webinar slides, 'illustrative for concept: not to scale'): HBM per GPU up 3.6x from H100 to B300 (per NVIDIA product specifications, H100 SXM 80GB HBM3 to Blackwell Ultra B300 288GB HBM3E) for training; memory per server up 2x in three years for inference and reasoning; AI context length growing 30x per year for agentic AI; and more than 10x the DRAM in an L4+ robotaxi versus today's L2+ car for physical AI. Micron: 'Memory has become the AI bottleneck'.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM per GPU 3.6x (H100 to B300); memory per server 2x in three years; context length 30x per year; >10x DRAM in L4+ robotaxi vs L2+ car

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: NAND roadmap (webinar slides): the next node, G11, is called 'the world's most advanced NAND' (Micron's claim), built with wafer-on-wafer bonding, more than 400 layers and industry-leading cell pitch, with 'Volume ramp in 2H 2027'. Versus G9, G11 targets about 2x bit density, up to 1.5x I/O speed and more than 25% less data transfer energy per bit. Beyond G11 Micron is working on a breakthrough high-mobility material, an ultra-dense cell architecture and energy-efficient devices and data paths.
quarterly_data.figure: G11: >400 layers; volume ramp in 2H 2027; ~2x bit density vs. G9; up to 1.5x I/O speed; >25% less data transfer energy per bit

players.product: 9550/6550 ION PCIe Gen5 enterprise & 61TB QLC SSD

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI-class NAND and future AI-optimized storage (webinar slides): Micron describes high-IOPS SLC NAND designs for GPU-initiated, small-block data access beyond system memory, and high-bandwidth AI-class NAND -- TSV-stacked NAND with a logic base die that enables a high-capacity tier close to the accelerator -- for model weights, long context and KV cache. Its future storage solutions include next-generation SSDs with high performance and high capacity (up to 512TB) and high-IOPS products with 25M-100M IOPS small-block access, plus storage for on-prem AI, AI PCs, automotive, humanoid robotics and mobile / wearables.
quarterly_data.figure: future SSDs up to 512TB; 25M-100M IOPS small-block access

quarterly_data.quarter: Micron IR presentation: Technology and product webinar (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Joint solution with WEKA (webinar slides): Micron 6600 ION 245TB SSDs deliver 15.8PB per 2U server; the joint solution reaches more than 1.1 EB in a single rack, and engineering-level SSD and platform optimization preserves power and space for more compute and, per Micron, delivers more than 2.1x throughput density versus competitors (both footnoted: WEKA NeuralMesh data reduction, assuming 3:1; results depend on configuration and workload).
quarterly_data.figure: 15.8PB per 2U server; >1.1 EB in a single rack; >2.1x throughput density vs. competitors
